concern: Modified nucleoside analogs with broad RNA polymerase inhibition
system_prompt: You are an expert computational medicinal chemist. Always respond with valid JSON containing a 'modifications' list. Each modification must include 'description', 'smiles', and 'rationale' fields.

modifications.description: Replace the phenyl group with a 3-fluorophenyl group to enhance pi-stacking interactions with RdRp aromatic residues
modifications.rationale: The addition of a fluorine atom to the phenyl ring can enhance pi-stacking interactions with aromatic residues in the RdRp active site, potentially improving binding affinity and selectivity.

modifications.description: Introduce a 2'-fluoro modification on the ribose sugar to increase steric complementarity with RdRp
modifications.rationale: The 2'-fluoro modification on the ribose sugar can enhance binding by forming additional polar interactions with the RdRp enzyme and improve stability against enzymatic degradation.

modifications.description: Add a methyl group to the terminal hydroxyl group of the ribose sugar to improve binding specificity
modifications.rationale: Methylation of the terminal hydroxyl group can enhance hydrophobic interactions with hydrophobic pockets in the RdRp enzyme, potentially improving specificity and potency.

modifications.description: Introduce a cyclopropyl group on the alkyl tail to increase hydrophobic contacts with nonpolar regions of RdRp
modifications.rationale: Replacing the linear alkyl chain with a cyclopropyl group increases hydrophobic interactions and rigidity, which can enhance binding affinity to nonpolar regions of RdRp.

modifications.description: Add an amide linker to the phenyl group to introduce hydrogen bonding interactions near the active site
modifications.rationale: The amide group can form hydrogen bonds with polar residues in the RdRp active site, potentially enhancing binding affinity and selectivity.
